en.title: Gaia Premium Development
en.description:
A landmark development in Vila Nova de Gaia, designed for those who value quality of life, comfort and a strategic location. More than simply a housing project, this development represents a genuine way of living, where contemporary architecture, practicality and wellbeing come together in balance.

Set in a privileged area close to Parque Municipal da Lavandeira, it enjoys surroundings that combine peace, nature and accessibility. Here you can enjoy a calm, well-ordered environment without giving up proximity to the centre of Porto, along with quick access to the main roads, shops, services and public transport.

Architecturally, the development stands out for its modern lines, well-defined massing and a striking aesthetic identity. The buildings were designed to maximise sun exposure, ensuring natural light throughout the day while safeguarding the privacy and comfort of residents. The integration with outdoor areas and green spaces reinforces the sense of harmony and quality of life.

In construction terms, this project sits clearly above average. The materials and solutions chosen prioritise comfort and efficiency, with particular attention to thermal and acoustic insulation, high-performance window frames, electric shutters, optimised climate control and the integration of modern technology such as home automation. The commitment to energy efficiency, with a high rating, translates not only into greater comfort but also into a significant reduction in day-to-day energy costs.

The interiors have been carefully considered to meet the real needs of anyone looking for a functional, welcoming home. The rooms are generous and well laid out, with abundant natural light that enhances every space. The living areas are modern and free-flowing, while the fully fitted kitchens and generous balconies create a harmonious link between inside and out, ideal for relaxing or entertaining.

The development also offers a set of amenities that raise the living experience to another level. As a gated community, it guarantees greater security and privacy, complemented by communal areas designed for residents’ wellbeing, such as landscaped grounds, outdoor walkways and social areas. Facilities including a residents’ lounge and a padel court reinforce the lifestyle concept behind this project.

With layouts ranging from one-bedroom apartments to larger options, the development suits a range of profiles, from young buyers looking for a first home to families or investors who value quality, location and growth potential.

In a city like Vila Nova de Gaia, growing and appreciating steadily, this project stands out as a solid opportunity, whether as a home or an investment. The combination of location, build quality and lifestyle makes this development a safe and distinctive choice in today’s market.

en.title: House with Pool in Guimarães
en.description:
This stunning detached four-bedroom house in Gonça, just 10 minutes from the centre of Guimarães, offers the perfect balance between peace, comfort and proximity to the region’s main towns and leisure spots. Set in a quiet area with excellent transport links, the house was designed to provide quality of life, privacy and wellbeing without giving up the convenience of being close to everything that matters.

With 200 m² of living space on a 479 m² plot, the house stands out for its luxury finishes and attention to detail throughout. On the main floor, the open-plan living room and kitchen enjoy an incredible view and natural light all day long, creating a sophisticated and welcoming atmosphere. The property also has three spacious en-suite bedrooms, an additional bedroom, a garage for two cars and an 8 m x 4 m swimming pool, perfect for memorable family moments.

The prime location adds to its value: as well as being just 10 minutes from the centre of Guimarães and from Póvoa de Lanhoso, it sits around 25 minutes from Gerês, the natural paradise of northern Portugal. If you are looking for a modern, practical home with a high level of comfort, this is a rare opportunity.

Globalead Portugal is on hand to support you throughout the purchase of this unique home, with personal guidance focused on your goals.

en.title: Three-Bedroom Apartment in Guimarães
en.description:
Exclusivity, natural light and panoramic views define this magnificent three-bedroom apartment in one of the most desirable and sought-after locations in Guimarães: the prestigious Salgueiral.

With 135 m² of living space, the property stands out for its generous rooms, excellent layout and exceptional light from three sun-facing aspects, which give a wide, open and truly unique view over the city. It currently has a comfortable master suite, and there is technical scope to create a second en-suite, offering greater flexibility to adapt to your family’s needs.

The comfort extends outdoors with a closed garage for two cars plus storage, totalling 49 m² of dependent gross area, an increasingly rare and valued addition. On the fourth floor of a modern building with two lifts, this apartment offers peace, privacy and a superior living experience.

The property is sold fully furnished and equipped, with a contemporary design and careful attention to detail, exactly as shown in the photographs, and is ready to move into with no further investment required.

The location is without doubt one of its greatest assets. In the heart of Salgueiral, it has all services, shops, schools and transport links within a few metres, while keeping the calm of an outstanding residential area considered one of the best addresses in Guimarães.

A distinctive property for anyone seeking quality, comfort and secure long-term value.

en.title: One-Bedroom Apartment, Lake Towers
en.description:
The one-bedroom apartment at Lake Towers is a unique opportunity to live in, or invest in, one of Porto’s new residential landmarks. Part of a modern development spread across four towers in Arca d’Água, on the site of the former Campo do Salgueiros, this project combines contemporary architecture, practicality and a genuinely strategic location.

With buildings of between 12 and 14 floors, Lake Towers brings together housing, student accommodation, retail space, services and a co-working area, creating a complete, dynamic and balanced urban environment. Living here means having everything on your doorstep without giving up peace and quiet.

This one-bedroom apartment was designed for the demands of contemporary life, with an intelligent layout that makes the most of every square metre. The T1 Smart layout stands out for its excellent natural light, modern lines and quality finishes, delivering comfort, efficiency and practicality day to day. Ideal for young professionals, students, a first home or an investment with strong rental potential, the apartment also enjoys a privileged view over Lago do Salgueiros, a distinctive feature that adds calm, value and exclusivity.

Being right next to Jardim de Arca d’Água adds further value, giving you generous green space and somewhere to relax, while benefiting from excellent transport links, shops, services and schools.

If you are looking for a modern, well-located apartment with strong growth potential in Porto, this one-bedroom at Lake Towers is a safe and strategic choice.

en.title: Gengibre Restaurant, Business for Sale
en.description:
An excellent business opportunity in the centre of Santo Tirso, in one of the busiest and most emblematic parts of the city: the well-known Praça dos Bares, in Largo Coronel Baptista Coelho. This is a very popular meeting point where, daily and above all at weekends, hundreds of people gather to socialise, dine and enjoy the nightlife.

The area takes on even greater prominence during the traditional Festas de São Bento, one of the city’s most important events, which draws thousands of visitors to this square every year.

Restaurante Gengibre is currently fully operational and has 17 years of trading under the same management, showing the stability and success the business has built over the years. It also has a strong takeaway arm through the Globo platform, ensuring a consistent flow of orders and an established revenue base.

Another highly attractive factor is the rent, one of the most competitive in the area, with an agreement in place to hold the current figure for the coming years, offering greater stability to whoever takes the business on.

The premises cover around 80 m² in total, with an indoor dining room seating approximately 50, a fully equipped kitchen, a bathroom, a storage area and a fitted counter. There is also a pleasant terrace seating around 40, with a timber deck and an electric roof, allowing use all year round.

With a prime location, constant footfall and an established customer base, this business has everything it needs to keep growing and become one of the most profitable in the area.

en.title: One-Bedroom Apartment in Santo Tirso
en.description:
Discover this modern one-bedroom apartment in the prestigious ARCO LIVING II development, in one of the most sought-after parts of Santo Tirso, right next to Hospital Trofa Saúde and part of a new urban centre growing fast.

The property stands out for its contemporary architecture, elegant lines and excellent use of space, designed to deliver comfort and practicality day to day. The living area is open-plan, with the kitchen and living room complementing each other to create a bright, spacious and inviting space, ideal both for relaxing and for entertaining.

The bedroom is comfortable and well proportioned, with fitted wardrobes providing practical storage. The bathroom has a modern, functional design in keeping with the quality of the finishes throughout the apartment. There is also a balcony, adding a connection to the outdoors and somewhere to enjoy a quiet moment, plus a garage space for everyday convenience.

In a recent building with a lift, this one-bedroom apartment enjoys excellent sun exposure and a privileged urban setting, with everything you need a few steps away. Being close to Hospital Trofa Saúde, as well as supermarkets, schools, services and quick access to the main roads, makes this location extremely practical and desirable.

The ARCO LIVING II development is part of the regeneration of a former industrial area, now transformed into a modern, dynamic and steadily appreciating district, making it one of the most sought-after places to live and invest in Santo Tirso.

This apartment is an excellent opportunity, whether as a home, particularly for anyone looking for a quality first property in a good location, or as an investment, benefiting from high demand in the area and strong growth potential.

en.title: Four-Bedroom House in Vila do Conde
en.description:
Some properties offer space. Others offer potential. This house offers both. Set on a generous 1,480 m² plot, this detached house with four elevations stands out for its versatility, privacy and excellent location. In a quiet residential area of Gião, Vila do Conde, it enjoys fast access to the A28, giving a comfortable link to the region’s main towns without giving up the calm of a family setting.

The grounds are one of its greatest assets. The large plot, green areas and outdoor space offer countless possibilities for anyone wanting to create a large garden, build a pool, set up an entertaining area or simply enjoy somewhere that is private throughout.

On the main floor, the house has two large rooms, a living room and a dining room, both with excellent sun exposure and generous proportions. The layout also allows for a modern open-plan area linking the living room to the kitchen, adapting the home to today’s expectations. The kitchen is fully fitted and equipped, ready to use, and there is also a cloakroom and a study, ideal for anyone who needs a dedicated space for working from home.

The private quarters are on the upper floor, with three bedrooms, one of them a comfortable en-suite with a fitted wardrobe and a full bathroom with a shower. The remaining bedrooms are served by a second full bathroom with a whirlpool bath. Every room has a balcony, providing excellent natural light throughout the day, along with thermal and security shutters that add to comfort and efficiency.

Designed with energy efficiency in mind, the house also has pre-installation for central heating, ready to work alongside the existing solar panels to reduce consumption without compromising comfort.

One of the features that adds most value is the self-contained floor. Comprising a bedroom with a fitted wardrobe, a living room, a fully equipped kitchen and a full bathroom, it is the ideal solution for a family wanting complete independence between generations, for hosting relatives or for creating rental income.

The basement holds a closed garage for four cars, complemented by a large storage area, providing everything needed day to day.

If you are looking for a house where space, location and versatility genuinely make the difference, this is a rare opportunity on the market. A property ready to meet today’s needs, with enormous potential for the future.

en.title: Two-Bedroom Apartment in Vila das Aves
en.description:
Some locations make all the difference. This is one of them. In the centre of Vila das Aves, this two-bedroom apartment lets you live with everything a few minutes’ walk away. Bakeries, cafés, supermarkets, banks, the post office, schools, shops and the main services are practically on your doorstep, making everyday life simpler, more practical and more comfortable.

With around 100 m², two aspects with excellent sun exposure (east/west) and built by Pacoli, one of the most respected construction companies in the country, the property stands out for the quality of its finishes, the practicality of its layout and the soundness of its build.

The living area was designed for comfort and sociability. The open-plan kitchen sits harmoniously alongside the living room, creating a bright, modern and spacious environment. For anyone who prefers greater separation, the kitchen can be closed off again. This space also has an enclosed laundry, a wine store and several fitted cupboards, offering excellent storage.

The living room is large and welcoming, with a wood-burning stove and access to two balconies with an open view, providing excellent natural light throughout the day.

The private area has two good-sized bedrooms, both with fitted wardrobes and a balcony, served by a full bathroom.

For added convenience, the apartment also has a garage space and a storage room.

If you are looking for an apartment where a prime location, build quality and a practical layout come together to deliver an excellent quality of life, this could be the opportunity you have been waiting for.

en.title: Four-Bedroom House in Guimarães
en.description:
In the heart of one of Portugal’s most emblematic cities, this house is a unique opportunity for anyone seeking sophistication, comfort and privacy.

Located in the prestigious city of Guimarães, this semi-detached house combines closeness to city life with the calm of a genuine private retreat, where the garden, the pool and the outdoor spaces were designed to deliver quality of life at every moment.

With modern, minimalist architecture and around 320 m² of built area, the property is currently at the finishing stage, which still leaves room to personalise some details so you can adapt the house to your lifestyle and turn it into the home you always imagined.

On the ground floor, practicality takes the lead. Here you will find a closed garage with natural light and access to an interior courtyard, a laundry, a plant room and a full bathroom. This floor also has a versatile, light-filled multi-purpose space, ideal for creating an additional bedroom, a study, a quieter sitting room or a family area.

The first floor is the true social heart of the house. The large living and dining room flows into a modern kitchen, creating an elegant, practical space designed for daily life. This floor also has a cloakroom and a magnificent covered terrace with direct access to the pool area, perfect for time with family and friends, always with the privacy a house like this demands.

The second floor holds the most private part of the house, with three bedrooms, including a master suite with its own balcony. The remaining bedrooms are served by a full bathroom, ensuring comfort and practicality for the whole family.

This property stands out for the harmony between contemporary architecture, thermal and acoustic comfort, private outdoor space and a prime location in Guimarães.

A house for anyone who values design, exclusivity and quality of life.

en.title: Two-Bedroom Apartment in Moreira, Maia
en.description:
A two-bedroom apartment of 108 m² in Moreira, Maia, in a quiet, privileged residential area with easy access to shops, services and the main roads. The location is one of this property’s great strengths, in an area of growing demand thanks to its proximity and easy access to Porto, Trofa, Vila Nova de Famalicão and Santo Tirso, as well as Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport.

On entering the apartment you are met by a hall that distributes the space well, separating the living area from the private quarters. The living area has a fitted and equipped kitchen with access to an enclosed balcony, currently used as a laundry, and to a pantry, providing extra storage and support space.

The living room stands out for its size and light, with a wood-burning stove and direct access to an unusually large balcony with an open view over the city. This outdoor space is ideal for enjoying time with family or simply relaxing, and is one of the apartment’s great assets.

The whole property has central heating for greater everyday comfort. Sun exposure is another of its strengths, as the apartment has two aspects, allowing excellent natural light throughout the day.

The private area has a corridor with several fitted cupboards, offering excellent storage. The apartment has two bedrooms, one of them en-suite with a recently renovated, practical private bathroom and fitted wardrobes. There is also a second full bathroom serving the other bedroom and the living area.

In addition, the apartment has a storage room and a garage space for one car, with the possibility of a second space.

This apartment stands out for its excellent layout, natural light, generous proportions, storage, comfort and, above all, its strategic location, combining the calm of a residential area with proximity to the main urban centres, services and road links.

en.title: Renovation Opportunity
en.description:
If you are looking for an opportunity with room for value growth, development flexibility and strong return potential, this property deserves your attention.

It is a freehold plot of 1,216 m², currently comprising four semi-detached one-bedroom houses requiring full reconstruction. The layout allows a renovation project tailored to today’s market, with scope to create one-bedroom or one-bedroom-plus houses, extend the built area at the rear of the plot, and even separate off a parcel to build a detached house with four elevations and its own entrance.

This versatility opens up different investment strategies, whether renovating and reselling the homes, letting them long-term or a combination of both, benefiting from growing demand for practical, well-located housing.

Located in Serzedelo, Guimarães, next to Riba d’Ave, the property is around 2 km from the motorway access, in a residential area with good transport links and close to shops, services and the region’s main urban centres.

In a market where opportunities with genuine capacity for transformation are increasingly rare, this project stands out for its development and growth potential over the medium and long term.

en.title: Trofa Premium Development
en.description:
Trofa is today one of the towns with the greatest growth potential in northern Portugal. In full urban expansion, with new investment, residential development and rising property demand, it is establishing itself as one of the most promising markets for anyone seeking quality of life alongside secure long-term value. Here, dynamism sits in perfect harmony with the calm, safety and family atmosphere that characterise the town.

Strategically located between Porto and Braga, with excellent road and rail links, Trofa stands out for its easy connection to the region’s main cities, making it a smart choice to live in or invest in.

It is against this backdrop of growth that Trofa Premium is born.

Facing the Trofense stadium, in a central, established part of town, the development enjoys a complete setting, with supermarkets, schools, pharmacies, services and shops minutes away, plus fast access to the main roads linking the surrounding towns. A location that combines convenience, mobility and strong future growth potential.

Trofa Premium is a modern, sophisticated development, conceived for those seeking more than a home: comfort, exclusivity and a secure bet on the future. With contemporary architectural lines and a distinctive concept, it stands out for the balance between bold design, practicality and sustainability.

Every detail has been considered to deliver energy efficiency, elegance and wellbeing, creating spaces that raise the experience of living. Here, modernity is allied to technology and build quality, ensuring not only daily comfort but also solid growth potential.

If you would like more detail about this development, its terms, layouts or prices, Globalead Portugal is ready to support you throughout the process. From analysing the investment to mortgage brokerage, we help find the best financing, comparing bank offers and securing the most advantageous terms for you.

Trofa Premium is not just a development. It is an opportunity.

And Globalead Portugal is beside you to turn that opportunity into a secure, well-structured decision.

en.title: Chaminé Development
en.description:
A new residential development is taking shape in Trofa that promises to raise the standard of living in the town, combining contemporary architecture, comfort and a strategic location in a fast-growing area.

The project sits next to the new public health centre and benefits from modern, convenient access, notably via the EN14 bypass linking Trofa to Maia and Vila Nova de Famalicão, reinforcing its central position and accessibility.

The development was designed as a gated community, guaranteeing greater privacy and security, and comprises 36 units in one-, two- and three-bedroom layouts, plus one unit for retail or services. The building rises over three floors above ground with a basement for parking, plant rooms and communal space.

The architecture stands out for its modern lines and attention to detail, using superior materials that ensure durability and sophistication. Set within a low-density urban context, the project offers a calm and exclusive atmosphere, ideal for anyone who values quality of life.

In terms of comfort and daily living, the development was designed to promote wellbeing and a sense of community among residents, with outdoor space, green areas and communal areas that encourage time spent relaxing, socialising or simply enjoying the surroundings.

The apartments have well-distributed rooms, excellent natural light, generous balconies and a harmonious connection between interior spaces. The fitted kitchens, integrated into modern living areas, and the welcoming bedrooms were designed for practicality, comfort and quality day to day.

The location is another of its great strengths, giving fast access to schools, services, cultural venues and leisure areas within a radius of just 1 km, making this development ideal both for families and for anyone seeking proximity and convenience.

Taken together, this is a solid opportunity for anyone seeking a modern home in a peaceful setting, with excellent transport links and high growth potential.

en.title: Vila Jardim Development
en.description:
Vila Jardim, in Vila das Aves in the municipality of Santo Tirso, is born where the calm of nature meets the energy and growth of one of the most active regions in northern Portugal.

Surrounded by green space, the development offers an environment designed for anyone who values quality of life, wellbeing and contact with nature. Somewhere you can enjoy your leisure time, exercise or simply take in the peace that characterises the surroundings.

The location is another of Vila Jardim’s great strengths. Set in a region with strong economic and industrial energy, it enjoys excellent access to Porto, Braga and Guimarães, letting you combine the calm of a residential area with proximity to the main urban centres.

It is in this balance between nature, comfort and accessibility that Vila Jardim is born, a development designed to deliver a modern, practical and comfortable way of living.

With two- and three-bedroom apartments, the project presents contemporary architecture and carefully considered spaces that answer the needs of daily life. The apartments favour light, spaciousness and flow, with practical, integrated living areas and bedrooms designed for greater privacy and comfort.

More than a residential development, Vila Jardim sets out to offer a genuine way of living. The communal areas were designed to encourage community, wellbeing and a more sustainable life, including a gourmet room, bicycle storage and an organic garden.

The project also has garage parking, adding convenience, security and practicality to residents’ daily lives.

With a balanced combination of build quality, contemporary design, nature and a strategic location, Vila Jardim is an excellent option both for anyone looking for a new home and for anyone looking for an investment opportunity.

The development is due for completion in July 2027, with payment terms of 10% on signing the promissory contract (CPCV) and the remaining 90% on completion.

Vila Jardim. A place designed for living with more comfort, calm and quality.

en.title: Storm damage: banks launch special loans to rebuild homes
en.excerpt: Storm Kristin caused serious damage to homes, infrastructure and businesses across Portugal, prompting Caixa Geral de Depósitos and Novo Banco to launch special credit lines totalling 400 million euros to support affected families and businesses.
en.content:
Storm Kristin caused serious damage to homes, infrastructure and businesses across Portugal, prompting Caixa Geral de Depósitos and Novo Banco to launch special credit lines totalling 400 million euros to support affected families and businesses.

CGD has made 300 million euros available in extraordinary measures, including loans for repairs and renovation at 0% spread with no fees, moratoriums of up to six months, reduced interest on existing contracts and extended terms of up to ten years. The measures apply to new applications submitted by 31 March 2026.

Novo Banco has announced 100 million euros in subsidised credit lines for families repairing homes and for businesses restoring operations and infrastructure, also on more favourable terms such as zero spread and no fees.

Storm Kristin left at least six people dead, along with injuries and displaced residents, hitting the districts of Leiria, Coimbra and Santarém hardest. The Government declared a state of calamity for around 60 municipalities, a figure that may yet be extended.

en.title: Letting a property: rent guarantee insurance reduces the risk
en.excerpt: Portugal’s rental market is still marked by strong demand, high rents and short supply, leaving many landlords hesitant to put properties up for rent.
en.content:
Portugal’s rental market is still marked by strong demand, high rents and short supply, leaving many landlords hesitant to put properties up for rent. Chief among their concerns are missed rent payments, lengthy and costly eviction proceedings, repair costs and market instability, all of which directly affect a property’s return.

Added to these risks are the tax burden on rental income and the possibility of accumulated rent increases, which raise uncertainty for landlords and tenants alike.

Against this backdrop, rent guarantee insurance is proving an effective way to make letting safer. This type of cover guarantees payment of rent arrears, provides legal protection, often includes an upfront assessment of the tenant’s creditworthiness, and gives the landlord greater financial predictability.

In a volatile and demanding market, taking out rent guarantee insurance can be a prudent strategy to reduce risk, keep properties on the rental market and secure long-term stability.

en.title: Rental support in 2026: what actually changes?
en.excerpt: In 2026, rental support in Portugal centres mainly on tax incentives to increase supply and hold prices down. The headline measures are a reduction in income tax to 10% on rental income from contracts with rents up to €2,300, and an increase in the tenant income tax deduction to €900 a year.
en.content:
In 2026, rental support in Portugal centres mainly on tax incentives to increase supply and hold prices down. The headline measures are a reduction in income tax to 10% on rental income from contracts with rents up to €2,300, and an increase in the tenant income tax deduction to €900 a year.

For tenants, direct support for households struggling to pay rent continues and is being strengthened through the IHRU, while the Porta 65 Jovem and Porta 65+ programmes remain active with more flexible rules. The Extraordinary Rent Support scheme keeps monthly payments of up to €200 for households with a high rent-to-income ratio.

For landlords, alongside the income tax reduction, the plans include VAT at 6% on the construction of affordable rental housing, exemption from capital gains tax where sale proceeds are reinvested in this type of property, and the creation of long-term investment contracts for rental housing.

Other measures include cutting red tape in planning permission, strengthening public-private partnerships and bringing vacant properties into the affordable rental scheme. Rents may be increased by up to 2.24%, in line with inflation, with no new extraordinary caps.

The overall aim is clear: increase the supply of housing, encourage moderate rents and bring greater stability to the rental market.

en.title: Luxury property in Portugal keeps growing in 2026
en.excerpt: The luxury property segment is expected to keep growing in 2026, having outperformed the mainstream market in both sales volume and value in 2025, according to the Luxury Outlook 2026 report from Portugal Sotheby’s International Realty.
en.content:
The luxury property segment is expected to keep growing in 2026, having outperformed the mainstream market in both sales volume and value in 2025, according to the Luxury Outlook 2026 report from Portugal Sotheby’s International Realty. The report points to the intergenerational transfer of wealth, estimated at 6 trillion dollars, as one of the main drivers of this demand, in a segment less exposed to economic swings.

The study also finds supply returning to more balanced levels, close to the pre-pandemic period, creating more opportunities for buyers, investors and sellers, particularly at the premium end.

Portugal features prominently in the European luxury property landscape, with sustained growth in transactions and in the development of new residential projects. Lisbon remains the main hub, but Cascais, Porto, the Algarve, Madeira and emerging areas such as Comporta are gaining ground with domestic and international buyers alike.

The report also highlights rising demand for branded residences, homes built around lifestyle, wellbeing and integrated services, as well as a greater emphasis on security and on homes suited to multigenerational families.

In an increasingly demanding global market, luxury property is confirming itself as a resilient and continually evolving segment, with Portugal well placed to attract high-value international investment.

en.title: Construction sector grows but structural weaknesses remain
en.excerpt: Portugal’s construction sector is enjoying a favourable economic moment, with growth, high demand and positive expectations for 2025. Even so, it continues to show deep structural weaknesses, according to the 2025 Construction Industry Barometer produced by Fundação Mestre Casais in partnership with AICCOPN.
en.content:
Portugal’s construction sector is enjoying a favourable economic moment, with growth, high demand and positive expectations for 2025. Even so, it continues to show deep structural weaknesses, according to the 2025 Construction Industry Barometer produced by Fundação Mestre Casais in partnership with AICCOPN.

The study concludes that although 100% of companies expect growth and 88% expect to meet or exceed their targets, that momentum rests largely on immediate demand, particularly in the residential segment, rather than on structural productivity gains. The sector is growing, but “on fragile foundations”.

The main obstacles identified are the small size of companies, weak internationalisation, a shortage of skilled labour and an ageing workforce, all of which limit capacity to deliver and to innovate. Most companies remain focused on the domestic market, with 60% having no international activity at all.

CEO confidence in the political and institutional environment is falling, reflecting criticism of public housing policy and of investment in infrastructure. Current growth is driven mainly by the private market, above all housing, rather than by public strategy.

While companies acknowledge the importance of innovation, digitalisation and sustainability, only a small percentage have taken concrete steps in these areas. In most cases sustainability is still treated as a reputational requirement rather than an integrated operating model.

en.title: Transform your outdoor space and add value to your home
en.excerpt: An outdoor kitchen today is far more than somewhere to barbecue. It is a genuine extension of the house, designed to bring comfort, sociability and a new way of living in your outdoor space, whether that is a garden, a terrace or a courtyard.
en.content:
An outdoor kitchen today is far more than somewhere to barbecue. It is a genuine extension of the house, designed to bring comfort, sociability and a new way of living in your outdoor space, whether that is a garden, a terrace or a courtyard.

Before starting work, it is essential to decide how the space will be used. A practical outdoor kitchen should include areas for preparation, cooking and support, keeping it easy to use day to day. Being close to the indoor kitchen also matters.

The choice of materials determines how long the space will last. Options such as stone, concrete, technical ceramics or stainless steel offer greater resistance to the elements, while timber can be used provided it is properly treated.



On equipment, the traditional grill remains central, but it can be complemented with a hob, an oven, a fridge or a sink, depending on how often you will use it. Organisation and storage are also essential to keep things practical and avoid constant trips back indoors.

To make the space comfortable all year round, solutions such as pergolas or awnings help create shade and improve the experience.

In investment terms, costs can range from around €1,500 for simpler solutions to more than €10,000 for complete, integrated projects, depending on the level of customisation and the equipment chosen.

A well-planned outdoor kitchen not only improves quality of life, it can also significantly increase the value of your property.

en.title: 6% VAT on housing: a construction incentive with new obligations
en.excerpt: The Government’s housing tax package introduces 6% VAT on the construction of homes intended as a main and permanent residence, provided the values involved are considered moderate. The main aim is to stimulate housing supply in Portugal and help address the growing difficulty of accessing housing.
en.content:
The Government’s housing tax package introduces 6% VAT on the construction of homes intended as a main and permanent residence, provided the values involved are considered moderate. The main aim is to stimulate housing supply in Portugal and help address the growing difficulty of accessing housing.

The new regime does, however, come with stricter rules for anyone benefiting from the incentive. Buyers purchasing property at the reduced VAT rate are required to use it as their main and permanent residence for at least 12 months. If that condition is not met, whether through an early sale or a change of use, a significant tax penalty applies.

In those cases the buyer will face a 10 percentage point increase in Property Transfer Tax (IMT), calculated by reference to the time of purchase. This approach places responsibility for compliance on the buyer, avoiding penalties for developers or builders over decisions they do not control once the sale is done.

The construction and property sector sees the change as a balance between incentive and responsibility. For several industry representatives, the IMT penalty acts as a deterrent to speculative behaviour, ensuring the tax break serves its social purpose: making it easier to buy a main and permanent home.

Despite the new requirements, the VAT reduction to 6% is widely regarded as a positive structural measure, with the capacity to energise the market, encourage new housing projects and increase available supply, bringing it closer to the real needs of Portuguese families.

en.title: Renting gets cheaper again in Portugal: rents fall 2.9% in May
en.excerpt: Portugal’s rental market continues to show signs of adjustment. According to the latest figures from the idealista price index, residential rents fell 2.9% in May compared with the same period last year, extending a downward trend now running for four consecutive months.
en.content:
Portugal’s rental market continues to show signs of adjustment. According to the latest figures from the idealista price index, residential rents fell 2.9% in May compared with the same period last year, extending a downward trend now running for four consecutive months.

This comes after several years of sharp rent increases, driven by high demand and a shortage of available supply. Although the decline is visible nationally, the picture still varies significantly between regions and cities, with markets where rents remain high or are even continuing to rise.



Analysts point to several factors behind the trend, among them stronger demand in the sales market, supported by incentives to buy, along with signs of increased supply in certain parts of the country. Even so, the rental market still faces challenges around availability, as the stock of homes to rent remains below the level recorded a year ago.

Despite this fall in average prices, access to housing remains a concern for many Portuguese families. Regional differences are still pronounced, and the rents charged in the main urban centres continue to represent a significant burden for much of the population.

The coming months will be decisive in showing whether this downward trend holds or whether it is only a temporary adjustment after the record highs of recent years. For now, the data suggests renting in Portugal is slightly more affordable than a year ago, even if the market remains marked by strong local disparities.

en.title: IMT exemption: young buyers bought over 41,000 homes in 2025
en.excerpt: In 2025, the exemption from Property Transfer Tax (IMT) and Stamp Duty on a first home allowed almost 61,000 people under 35 to buy, across a total of 41,370 properties, according to Ministry of Finance figures.
en.content:
In 2025, the exemption from Property Transfer Tax (IMT) and Stamp Duty on a first home allowed almost 61,000 people under 35 to buy, across a total of 41,370 properties, according to Ministry of Finance figures. The average purchase price was 205,700 euros, with an average tax saving of 6,300 euros per property. Full exemption applied to homes up to 324,058 euros, while partial exemption covered properties up to 648,022 euros.

In January 2026, the Finance Minister, Joaquim Miranda Sarmento, updated the figures, reporting that more than 70,000 young people have now benefited from the IMT and Stamp Duty exemption, while the state mortgage guarantee has covered around 23,000 young buyers, with only one case of default recorded. These measures form part of the Government’s strategy to attract and retain human capital, alongside instruments such as the Youth Income Tax scheme.

Although studies, notably from ISCTE, suggest that demand-side measures may have contributed to rising house prices, the minister rejected any direct link, arguing that the market’s main problem is a shortage of supply resulting from low construction levels.

The Youth IMT and Stamp Duty exemption was created in 2024 by Luís Montenegro’s first government and applies to people under 35 buying a first main and permanent home. The state guarantee, available on contracts signed up to the end of 2026, allows the State to guarantee up to 15% of the transaction value, giving young buyers access to financing of up to 100% of the property valuation rather than the general 90% limit.

en.title: Tenant right of first refusal: how does it work?
en.excerpt: When a landlord decides to sell a property that is being let, the tenant may have a right of first refusal on the purchase. That means the tenant can have priority to buy the property before it is sold to someone else.
en.content:
When a landlord decides to sell a property that is being let, the tenant may have a right of first refusal on the purchase. That means the tenant can have priority to buy the property before it is sold to a third party, provided certain conditions set out in law are met.

The right of first refusal is set out in article 1091 of the Civil Code and was strengthened by Law 64/2018 of 29 October. Broadly, it applies to tenants whose tenancy has run for more than two years.

To exercise the right, the tenant must have lived in the property for more than two years and intend to buy it as their own home. When the landlord decides to sell, they must notify the tenant of the terms of sale, including the price and the other conditions of the deal. From that notification, the tenant has 30 days to say whether or not they wish to exercise the right to buy.



The right of first refusal does not apply only to tenants, however. In some situations public bodies such as the State, municipal councils or autonomous regions may also have priority. This happens mainly where the property sits in an area under urban development pressure, in an urban regeneration area, or where it is classified as heritage of public interest.

Before proceeding with a sale, the owner should check whether the property is subject to this regime. If it is, the intention to sell must be published on the Casa Pronta portal, stating the property details, the parties to the deal, the agreed price and the expected transaction date.

After publication, public bodies have 10 working days to decide whether to exercise the right. If they do not do so within that period, the owner may proceed with the sale to the originally intended buyer.

The right of first refusal is designed to protect tenants and bring greater balance to the housing market, while allowing the State to intervene in preserving heritage and managing land use.

en.title: Selling my home: do I need an energy certificate?
en.excerpt: If you are thinking of selling or letting your home, an energy certificate is mandatory. This document rates the property’s energy efficiency on a scale from A+ (very efficient) to F (poor) and is issued by assessors authorised by the Portuguese Energy Agency (ADENE).
en.content:
Do I need an energy certificate to sell or let my home?

If you are thinking of selling or letting your home, an energy certificate is mandatory. This document rates the property’s energy efficiency on a scale from A+ (very efficient) to F (poor) and is issued by assessors authorised by the Portuguese Energy Agency (ADENE).

The certificate is required whenever a property is marketed for sale or rent, and applies to:

  • New buildings;
  • Buildings undergoing major renovation;
  • Commercial and service properties over 1,000 m² (or 500 m² in shopping centres, supermarkets and indoor pools);
  • Public buildings frequently visited by the public and over 250 m²;
  • Any property at the point of sale, letting or transfer;
  • Buildings taking part in funding programmes or tax benefits that require certification.

Having this certificate is not only a legal obligation, it also tells buyers or tenants how energy efficient the home is, which can add value on the market.


Get your energy certificate with Globalead Portugal

The energy certificate is an official document that assesses a property’s energy efficiency, assigning a rating from A+ to F and setting out recommendations for possible improvements, including estimated savings. It is issued by qualified ADENE assessors under the Building Certification System (SCE) and governed by Decree-Law 101-D/2020.

en.title: A pool at home: do you need a licence or prior notification?
en.excerpt: Having a pool at home is a dream for many families. As well as bringing comfort and enjoyment through the warmer months, it can also add value to the property. Before starting any work, however, it is essential to know the legal rules and the procedures involved.
en.content:
Having a pool at home remains one of the most sought-after investments for anyone looking for more comfort, more enjoyment and added value. Before starting any work, though, it is important to understand the rules currently in force and which procedures must be followed to avoid problems later on.

The legislation has changed in recent years, and many people have come away with the impression that no authorisation of any kind is now needed to build a pool. In reality, although planning permission is no longer required in many cases, that does not mean work can start without any formality. Construction is still subject to prior notification to the relevant municipal council, and a set of technical documents must be submitted so that the project can be checked against all applicable planning rules.

Before proceeding, it is equally important to confirm that the land meets the conditions for this type of construction. That check matters even more where the property sits on rural land, since restrictions imposed by the Municipal Master Plan or by environmental constraints may rule the work out. For that reason, consulting the municipal council or a specialist in advance can avoid delays, unnecessary costs and possible enforcement proceedings.



Another aspect that is often overlooked is the effect a pool can have on the property’s tax position. As it is considered to add value to the home, building one can feed through to the Rateable Value (VPT), which may in turn increase Municipal Property Tax (IMI). While the increase varies case by case, it is a factor to build into the investment plan.

Beyond the legal and tax questions, it is also worth spending time planning the pool itself. The choice of construction type, its position on the plot and the equipment installed affect not only the initial cost but also future spending on maintenance, energy and day-to-day use. A well-planned pool can be a significant asset to the property and deliver a better quality of life for many years.

In short, building a pool remains an excellent investment, but it requires preparation and an understanding of the rules in force. Getting informed in advance, making sure all the paperwork is in order and assessing the financial impact of the work are essential steps to keep the project free of surprises and within the law.

en.title: Banco de Portugal prepares new mortgage rules
en.excerpt: Banco de Portugal is preparing a new set of measures that could make mortgages harder to obtain over the coming months. The aim is to curb rising household debt and reduce the risks to the financial system and the property market.
en.content:
Banco de Portugal is preparing a new set of measures that could make mortgages harder to obtain over the coming months. The aim is to curb rising household debt and reduce the risks to the financial system and the property market.

Mortgage lending has grown significantly again in recent years, driven largely by the state guarantee created for buyers under 35. That measure allowed many buyers to borrow more than 90% of a property’s value, something previously restricted by Banco de Portugal’s rules. As a result, the number of higher-risk contracts has risen, with many households financing almost the entire purchase through the bank.

One of the main changes under consideration is an increase in the so-called stress rate, the mechanism banks use to assess whether customers could keep up repayments if interest rates were to rise. Banks currently run that simulation assuming a 1.5 percentage point increase, but Banco de Portugal is considering a return to levels close to 3%, as was previously the case. In practice, that means banks may become stricter in approving loans, reducing the maximum amount many households can borrow.



Alongside this change, the regulator may also revisit limits on lending relative to property value, known as the LTV ratio, as well as maximum loan terms. If these measures go ahead, many buyers are likely to need a larger deposit and to demonstrate stronger finances in order to be approved.

Banco de Portugal takes the view that rapid growth in mortgage lending, combined with steadily rising house prices, could create risks for households and for the banks themselves. At the same time, the Government continues to back measures supporting young buyers, including a strengthened state guarantee, creating some divergence in strategy between the two institutions. While the Government seeks to widen access to housing, Banco de Portugal wants to prevent excessive debt and further pressure on property prices.

For anyone planning to buy in the near future, these changes could mean tighter access to credit, more rigorous bank assessments and greater weight given to financial stability and the debt-to-income ratio when a loan is approved.

en.title: Young buyers and lower-income couples rely more on the state guarantee
en.excerpt: Access to housing remains one of Portugal’s greatest challenges, particularly for young people and lower-income families. Recent Banco de Portugal data reveals a clear trend: these groups are turning more and more to the state guarantee in order to buy a home.
en.content:
Access to housing remains one of Portugal’s greatest challenges, particularly for young people and lower-income families. Recent Banco de Portugal data reveals a clear trend: these groups are turning more and more to the state guarantee in order to buy a home.

According to the report, around 62% of loans granted under this scheme were taken out by two borrowers, showing that many buyers choose to share the burden in order to increase how much they can borrow. By contrast, among buyers who do not use the state guarantee, individual contracts are more common.

Lower incomes and a heavier financial burden

The data also shows that borrowers using the state guarantee have lower average incomes. For joint loans, average net income per person is 1,412 euros, compared with around 1,687 euros in other cases.

That difference feeds directly into the debt-to-income ratio. Those using the state guarantee face higher repayments as a proportion of income, reaching around 42.8% on individual contracts and 39% on joint ones, both above the levels recorded outside the scheme.



Younger buyers gain better access to credit

The introduction of the state guarantee has had a significant effect on the buyer profile. The share of borrowers aged up to 35 has risen from around 40% to 54%, reinforcing the scheme’s role in opening up access to housing for younger buyers.

Average loan amounts also differ: contracts backed by the state guarantee average around 207,000 euros, above the 174,000 euros seen in other cases.

An increasingly significant instrument in the market

In 2025 the state guarantee accounted for 15% of new mortgage contracts and almost 20% of the total amount lent. The State initially set a ceiling of 1,200 million euros, since raised to 1,550 million, of which more than half has already been used.

What does this mean if you want to buy?

The state guarantee has established itself as an important solution for anyone struggling to access a mortgage, particularly young people and families starting out. Even so, it is essential to look carefully at the debt-to-income ratio and make sure the commitment is sustainable over the long term.

At Globalead Portugal we follow these schemes closely and help each client find the best strategy, with or without the state guarantee, always with a focus on financial security and stability.

en.title: Short-term lets: what may change by the end of 2026?
en.excerpt: Short-term letting (Alojamento Local) is back in the spotlight with the entry into force of Decree-Law 151/2026 of 30 July, which introduces a set of temporary measures on how municipalities regulate the activity. It should be made clear from the outset that this legislation is not a general overhaul of the short-term letting regime. Its main purpose is to give certain municipalities more time to draw up or amend their own rules and, during that period, to allow them to maintain some restrictions on new registrations.
en.content:
Short-term lets: what may change by the end of 2026?

Short-term letting (Alojamento Local) is back in the spotlight with the entry into force of Decree-Law 151/2026 of 30 July, which introduces a set of temporary measures on how municipalities regulate the activity.

It should be made clear from the outset that this legislation is not a general overhaul of the short-term letting regime. Its main purpose is to give certain municipalities more time to draw up or amend their own rules and, during that period, to allow them to maintain some restrictions on new registrations.

The new rules apply to municipalities that had passed 1,000 registered short-term letting establishments by 31 December 2025 and that have not yet resolved how to regulate the activity. In those cases, councils now have until 31 December 2026 to draw up or amend their municipal regulations.

During this period, municipalities where a suspension of new registrations is already in place may, in certain circumstances, extend it exceptionally and on one occasion only. That decision must be taken by the Municipal Assembly, on a proposal from the Council, and only for the period considered necessary to complete the regulatory process.

The legislation also provides for a further exceptional suspension where a previous one has already ended by reaching the maximum period allowed by law. This too depends on a municipal decision and may not, under any circumstances, extend beyond 31 December 2026.

That does not mean, however, that every suspension must necessarily remain in force until the end of 2026. They may end sooner, in particular once the relevant municipal regulation comes into force, by decision of the Municipal Assembly, or when the period set for the suspension itself is reached.

One of the most pressing questions for current owners of short-term letting properties is whether these measures affect existing registrations. On this point the legislation establishes that the suspensions do not have retroactive effect. Properties validly registered before the relevant municipal resolution came into force keep their registrations, with the restrictions aimed essentially at new applications submitted afterwards.

For anyone looking to invest in a property for short-term letting, these changes underline the importance of checking the specific position of the property and the rules in force in the relevant municipality beforehand. Until the end of 2026 the picture may differ between municipalities, and even between different areas of the same municipality, depending on the regulations and any suspensions in force.

Before completing a purchase with this purpose in mind, it will therefore be particularly important to confirm that the property can be used for short-term letting, to know the applicable municipal regulation and to understand whether the location is covered by any restriction or suspension of new registrations.

In practical terms, Decree-Law 151/2026 creates a transitional regime that allows certain municipalities to complete their regulatory processes by the end of 2026, while giving them mechanisms to temporarily control the opening of new short-term letting properties.

For owners and investors, the main conclusion is clear: before buying a property to run as a short-term let, it is increasingly important to look not only at the property itself but also at the specific rules that apply to its location.

In a constantly evolving market, understanding the applicable framework in advance can be the difference between a well-structured investment opportunity and a decision based on assumptions that may not hold.

Source: Decree-Law 151/2026 of 30 July, Diário da República.

This content is for information only and is no substitute for consulting the legislation in force or obtaining legal advice appropriate to your specific situation.

en.title: I'm selling my home. Should I hire an estate agent?
en.excerpt: The role of a professional estate agent goes far beyond simply advertising the property. A good agent sets the right price based on real market data, filters buyers, avoids pointless viewings, manages negotiations and handles all the paperwork involved in the sale.
en.content:
In a market as hot as this one, with prices and transactions rising, it is tempting to sell your home without an estate agent. Is that a good idea?


Given the general perception of estate agents, and knowing the commission usually charged on a sale, it is indeed tempting for an owner to go it alone.

 

FSBO – For Sale by Owner is the term used for properties sold without an intermediary.

 

After all, how hard can it be to sell a house? Just put a listing on a property portal, share a few photos on social media and you are done. Isn’t that all an estate agent does? Why pay so much money for it?


So what does an estate agent actually do?


Or, at least, what should an estate agent do? Anyone who is a genuine professional, who treats the work as a profession and invests in it, will not simply put a few photographs online to sell a property.


An estate agent’s work, done well, is significant and takes a weight off the owner’s shoulders. The agent sets the right price for the property, qualifies potential buyers and so avoids unnecessary and ill-advised viewings, handles the viewings themselves and runs the negotiation. That is before mentioning all the paperwork required, and there is plenty of it, to sell a property.

 

For all of that to happen, an estate agent needs a set of important skills, among others:

  • A deep knowledge of the market or markets they work in;
  • A clear grasp of the reality, at any given moment, of local supply and demand;
  • Analytical ability, with command of the critical factors in a property’s success;
  • An understanding of the importance of external factors that shape a property’s price and sale;
  • An eye for the qualitative factors that add most value to a particular property in a specific location;
  • A complete focus on client service, investing in the relationship, in providing information and in following the process through.

In listing and selling a property, an estate agent should fundamentally be able to:

  • Advise, backed by real market data, on the right transaction price;
  • Present a marketing plan for the property, justifying the channels and materials to be used;
  • Advise on preparing the property for sale;
  • Pre-qualify every potential buyer;
  • Conduct every viewing;
  • Report back to the client regularly;
  • Always seek to defend the interests of the owner who is, after all, the one paying for the service.

If, in the end, the property sells at the price the owner wanted and within a reasonable time, is the commission really that high?

en.title: Portugal has become attractive to the global middle classes
en.excerpt: High housing prices in Portugal are the result of the country making its 'land' attractive to the global middle classes, pushing it to prices out of reach for the salaries paid in Portugal.
en.content:
The economist Félix Ribeiro argues that today’s high housing prices in Portugal are a direct consequence of the internationalisation of Portuguese land. As he explains, the country has become highly attractive to the global middle classes, both to live in and to invest in, which has brought Portuguese “land” onto the international market and pushed its value to prices that domestic salaries cannot keep up with.

In an interview with the Lusa news agency, Félix Ribeiro says Portugal “appeared on the radar” of large international operators, who began looking for land and property aimed at foreign buyers. The phenomenon has profoundly changed the Portuguese economy, turning what he calls the “land complex” – construction, property and tourism (hotels, resorts, golf courses and the rest) – into the dominant sector of the national economy.

Even the construction sector, which historically worked mainly for the domestic market, has reoriented itself towards this global market, contributing to the rapid appreciation of land and, consequently, to the sharp rise in housing prices. For the economist, this internationalisation of land has completely changed how properties are valued, explaining the escalation of house prices in Portugal.

That growth has not been matched by wages, however, creating a deep imbalance between the cost of housing and household income. Félix Ribeiro considers that the Portuguese economy “is not working in an integrated way”, which widens the gap further and makes it hard to correct without public intervention.


Source: Unsplash


In his view, the State will have to play an active role in easing the problem, for example by capitalising Social Security and putting it to work for housing as well. Without that involvement, the mismatch between prices and incomes is likely to persist.

Figures from the National Statistics Institute (INE) reinforce the analysis: in the third quarter of 2025, the median price of homes sold in Portugal rose 16.6% year on year, reaching 2,111 euros per square metre.

Asked about the labour reforms proposed by the Government, Félix Ribeiro stresses that the main obstacle to the Portuguese economy is not wages but the financial system. In his opinion, Portugal depends excessively on commercial banking, which is oriented above all towards financing property, and lacks a genuine capital market capable of supporting the transformation and diversification of the country’s productive structure.

For the economist, without structural change to the economic and financial model, Portugal will continue to struggle to provide affordable housing for the people who live and work here.

en.title: More people are asking for help to pay the rent in Portugal
en.excerpt: Access to housing in Portugal continues to worsen and is already regarded by several social organisations as one of the greatest social challenges of our time. Recent data analysed by Cáritas Portuguesa indicates that more and more people are seeking help to pay the rent, a reality the organisation describes as “a serious social problem”.
en.content:
Access to housing in Portugal continues to worsen and is already regarded by several social organisations as one of the greatest social challenges of our time. Recent data analysed by Cáritas Portuguesa indicates that more and more people are seeking help to pay the rent, a reality the organisation describes as “a serious social problem”.

One of the most worrying indicators is the significant rise in homelessness. In 2018, an estimated six thousand people were living in that situation in Portugal. Last year the figure rose to around 14,500, reflecting the worsening housing difficulties across the country.

Much of the problem is tied to how the property market has evolved. Between the start of 2020 and the third quarter of 2025, the median price per square metre of housing rose 74.3%, far outstripping nominal household disposable income, which grew around 45% over the same period. That gap intensifies pressure on family budgets and makes housing harder to access.

Difficulty finding affordable housing also helps explain why so many young people in Portugal continue to live with their parents compared with other European countries. According to the Cáritas analysis, 6.9% of Portuguese people are currently overburdened by housing costs, meaning rent or mortgage payments exceed 40% of household income. Before the pandemic that figure was 5.7%. Among those on the lowest incomes the situation is more worrying still, affecting 24.1% of people.



Another growing phenomenon is overcrowding, which affects around 11.2% of the Portuguese population. This indicator worsened above all after the pandemic and may be higher in reality, since many immigrants face severe difficulties accessing housing and are not always captured in official statistics.

Despite these challenges, some indicators show a slight overall improvement in the fight against poverty. The population at risk of poverty fell from 16.2% in 2019 to 15.4% in 2024, while the number of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion dropped from 2.7 million in 2015 to around two million in 2025.

Extreme situations of social exclusion persist, however. In 2025, more than a million people were living in material and social deprivation, around 460,000 of them in severe deprivation. These conditions directly affect access to basic necessities and make full participation in society harder.

Further data shows that around 200,000 people cannot afford an adequate diet, while 600,000 cannot afford to buy new clothes and 1.6 million lack the means to heat their home properly in winter.

According to Cáritas, even where some indicators are improving, progress is too slow to match the scale of the problem, reinforcing the need for structural policies that widen access to affordable housing and support the most vulnerable families.

The housing crisis therefore remains central to the social debate in Portugal, with a direct impact on quality of life, on the economic stability of families and on the future of coming generations.

en.title: Portugal has the 4th highest annual house price growth
en.excerpt: The Portuguese property market has again stood out internationally. In the first quarter of 2026, house prices in Portugal recorded nominal annual growth of 16.5%, placing the country fourth among the markets covered by Knight Frank’s international Global House Price Index.
en.content:
In the first quarter of 2026, Portugal recorded one of the highest rates of house price growth in the world. Prices rose 16.5% year on year, placing the country fourth among the 55 markets analysed by Knight Frank.

Even after inflation, real growth was 13.4%, well above the euro area and European Union averages. Eurostat data confirms the trend, pointing to a rise of 17.8%.

Despite the strong price growth, the number of transactions fell 8.7%, indicating a market still under pressure from demand but with some moderation in activity.

Why do house prices keep rising?

House price growth does not come down to a single factor. It results from a combination of elements that continue to put pressure on the Portuguese market.

One of the main factors is a shortage of supply. In many parts of the country, new construction and the number of properties coming to market have not kept pace with demand. When there are more interested buyers than available homes, prices naturally tend to rise.

Location also remains decisive. Properties close to urban centres, schools, services, transport and main road links continue to see high demand, particularly where they offer good proportions, build quality, parking and outdoor space.

Demand from international buyers also continues to matter, especially in the larger cities and in the upper-middle and luxury segments. Portugal retains its appeal thanks to quality of life, safety, stability, climate and its ability to attract buyers with high purchasing power.

At the same time, the cost of construction, labour, materials, land and planning processes continues to shape the final price of new properties, limiting how much more affordable supply reaches the market.



What does this growth mean if you want to sell?

For owners, this environment may be an opportunity to assess what the property is currently worth.

That said, national average growth of 16.5% or 17.8% does not mean every property has risen by exactly the same proportion. Prices behave differently according to location, layout, condition, build quality, proportions, energy efficiency, parking, outdoor space and demand in that particular area.

A well-located property, properly presented and sensibly priced, stands to benefit from current market conditions. A price set too high against comparable properties, by contrast, is likely to lengthen the time to sell and dampen buyer interest.

Before putting a property on the market, it is therefore important to base the analysis on properties that have actually sold, not simply on the prices advertised on the portals.

And if you want to buy?

For buyers, continued price growth makes careful financial preparation all the more important.

Before starting the search, it is essential to understand the real budget available, taking in not only the price of the home but also the deposit, taxes, completion costs, financing, insurance, service charges and any work needed.

In a market with limited supply, properties offering the best combination of price, location and condition can attract several enquiries or offers in a short space of time. Having your financing assessed in advance and knowing the limits of your budget allows for faster, safer decisions.

Even so, buying a home should not be a decision driven only by fear that prices will keep rising. It is important to weigh up long-term affordability, the characteristics of the property, the paperwork and the potential for future value or resale.

en.title: House prices in Portugal rise 16.8% in 2025 to €2,076/m²
en.excerpt: The Portuguese property market showed strong momentum again in 2025, with significant growth in house prices. According to figures released by the National Statistics Institute (INE), the median price of homes reached €2,076/m², a rise of 16.8% on 2024.
en.content:
The Portuguese property market maintained a path of strong growth in 2025, with the median price of homes reaching €2,076/m², a marked rise of 16.8% on 2024, according to National Statistics Institute figures. Over the year 164,677 transactions were completed, a volume showing that despite rising prices, demand remains high and consistent across practically the whole country.

That growth is not evenly spread. Regions such as Greater Lisbon, the Algarve, the Setúbal Peninsula, Madeira and the Porto Metropolitan Area continue to record values significantly above the national average, driven by domestic demand and, above all, by international interest. Lisbon remains the most expensive municipality in the country, with prices close to €4,875/m², followed by Cascais, Oeiras and several locations in the Algarve, where values easily exceed €3,500/m². At the same time, cities such as Vila Nova de Gaia and Porto continue to establish themselves as strategic alternatives, combining more competitive prices with strong growth potential.

In terms of market activity, Lisbon leads on the number of transactions, but municipalities such as Sintra, Vila Nova de Gaia and Porto also record substantial activity, pointing to a gradual shift in demand towards outlying and metropolitan areas. The trend is directly linked to the search for better value for money, greater availability and better living conditions.



Another decisive factor remains the weight of foreign buyers, who in many cases are prepared to pay more, adding to price pressure particularly in the upper-middle and premium segments. In Lisbon, for example, the prices paid by international buyers significantly exceed those paid by domestic buyers, reinforcing the competitiveness of the Portuguese market globally.

Alongside this, new-build properties continue to command higher prices than resale homes in most municipalities, reflecting growing demand for modern, efficient properties with better energy performance. The price gap between new build and resale is particularly evident in the large urban centres, where a shortage of new supply contributes to the growth in this segment.

In the final quarter of 2025, the median price rose to €2,198/m², growth of 17.5% on the same period a year earlier. Although the number of transactions dipped slightly, prices continued to rise in most regions, confirming the market’s resilience and the continued pressure of demand on still-limited supply.

Overall, these figures reflect a solid and growing property market, underpinned by structural factors such as the shortage of supply, Portugal’s international appeal, improving infrastructure and rising demand for quality of life. For anyone looking to buy, this picture reinforces the importance of acting in an informed and strategic way. For investors, significant opportunities remain, particularly in areas with strong potential for growth and urban development.

en.title: Trofa Premium: exclusivity in the centre of Trofa
en.excerpt: Trofa is today one of the towns with the greatest growth potential in northern Portugal. In full urban expansion, with new investment, residential development and rising property demand, it is establishing itself as one of the most promising markets for anyone seeking quality of life alongside secure long-term value. The town’s energy sits in perfect harmony with the calm, safety and family atmosphere that characterise it, making it increasingly attractive to families and investors alike.
en.content:
